_meta.indication: NEREUS is indicated for the prevention of vomiting induced by motion in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; subjects randomized 1:1:1 to a single oral dose of NEREUS 85 mg, 170 mg, or placebo ~60 minutes prior to a boat trip lasting ~2 to 5 hours.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of motion sickness on prior vehicle travel.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: percentage of subjects with vomiting during the boat trip (assessed every 30 minutes via a 1-item questionnaire).
pivotal_trials.result: Incidence of vomiting: 20% (85 mg) and 18% (170 mg) vs 44% placebo; treatment difference -25% (95% CI -36%, -14%) for 85 mg and -26% (95% CI -37%, -15%) for 170 mg.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 2 (also referred to as Trial 3404 in the review)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of a single oral dose of tradipitant 85 mg or 170 mg vs placebo in subjects with a history of motion sickness on prior vehicle travel.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of motion sickness on prior vehicle travel.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: percentage of subjects with vomiting during the boat trip (assessed every 30 minutes via a 1-item questionnaire).
pivotal_trials.result: Incidence of vomiting: 18% (85 mg) and 10% (170 mg) vs 38% placebo; treatment difference -19% (95% CI -31%, -8%) for 85 mg and -27% (95% CI -38%, -16%) for 170 mg.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are somnolence, headache, and fatigue. With NEREUS 170 mg: somnolence 12% vs 6% placebo, headache 10% vs 6% placebo, fatigue 8% vs 2% placebo.
target_moa: Tradipitant is a selective, high-affinity antagonist of human substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK-1) receptors; it crosses the blood brain barrier and occupies brain NK-1 receptors, inhibiting emesis.

boxed_warning.content: No boxed warning; the review states BOXED WARNING is Not applicable.

summary.text: NEREUS (tradipitant) was submitted as NDA 220152 by Vanda Pharmaceuticals on December 30, 2024 and approved for the prevention of vomiting induced by motion in adults; no special expedited designations (accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, priority) are stated in the documents, and approval was granted with postmarketing requirements/commitments and a labeled limitation that safety beyond 90 total doses has not been established.
